t: Google’s YouTube Kids App Presents Inappropriate Content
s: YouTube Kids showed children disturbing and inappropriate videos, such as familiar cartoon characters in violent scenes. Algorithmic filtering failed to catch them, and YouTube apologized.

t: Warehouse robot ruptures can of bear spray and injures workers
s: An automated machine at an Amazon warehouse in New Jersey punctured a can of bear repellent, releasing fumes that sent 24 workers to hospital and led dozens more to need treatment. One worker was in critical condition.

t: Crashes with Maneuvering Characteristics Augmentation System (MCAS)
s: A Lion Air Boeing 737 MAX crashed into the Java Sea, killing all 189 people aboard. Investigators found a faulty sensor repeatedly triggered an automated anti-stall system that forced the nose down while pilots struggled to regain control.

t: Uber AV Killed Pedestrian in Arizona
s: An Uber self-driving test vehicle struck and killed a woman crossing a street in Tempe, Arizona. Investigators reported the emergency braking was disabled and the safety driver was streaming video.

t: Collection of Robotic Surgery Malfunctions
s: A study of FDA reports from 2000 to 2013 found thousands of robotic surgery malfunctions, including 1,391 patient injuries and 144 deaths. Malfunctions included sparking instruments and pieces falling into patients.

t: Microsoft's TayBot Allegedly Posts Racist, Sexist, and Anti-Semitic Content to Twitter
s: Microsoft launched the Tay chatbot on Twitter, and within 24 hours it was taken offline after posting racist, sexist and anti-Semitic tweets learned from users' interactions.

t: Wikipedia Vandalism Prevention Bot Loop
s: Wikipedia's automated editing bots, each built to improve the encyclopedia, got locked in long-running loops of undoing one another's edits. A study found some of these conflicts lasted for years.

t: Uber Autonomous Cars Running Red Lights
s: Self-driving Uber cars ran red lights in San Francisco during street testing. Uber first blamed human error, but later reporting found the car's mapping software failed to recognize several traffic lights.

t: New York City Reportedly Released Disputed Value-Added Teacher Ratings for Thousands of Teachers
s: New York City released value-added ratings for thousands of public-school teachers based on estimated student test-score growth. Teachers, unions and analysts disputed the scores as imprecise and potentially misleading.

t: Kronos Scheduling Algorithm Allegedly Caused Financial Issues for Starbucks Employees
s: Scheduling software used by Starbucks managers reportedly produced erratic, last-minute work hours for baristas. Workers described disrupted childcare, education and finances, and managers blamed the software.

t: Northpointe Risk Models
s: A risk-scoring algorithm used in US courts and jails was found by a ProPublica analysis to wrongly label Black defendants as likely to reoffend at almost twice the rate of white defendants. The vendor disputes the findings.

t: Common Biases of Vector Embeddings
s: Researchers showed that widely used word embeddings trained on Google News text encode gender stereotypes, such as linking certain jobs more strongly with women or men. They proposed a method to reduce the bias.

t: High-Toxicity Assessed on Text Involving Women and Minority Groups
s: Google's Perspective tool, which scores how toxic online comments are, rated neutral statements mentioning minority identities as highly toxic while rating some hateful statements as safe.

t: Biased Sentiment Analysis
s: Google's Cloud Natural Language sentiment tool scored statements such as being gay or being Jewish as negative. Google acknowledged the bias, apologized and said it would improve the models.

t: Amazon Censors Gay Books
s: Hundreds of gay and lesbian themed books lost their sales rankings on Amazon, reducing their visibility. Amazon blamed a cataloging error, while critics suspected an adult-content policy applied to LGBT titles.

t: Images of Black People Labeled as Gorillas
s: Google Photos' automatic image labeling tagged photos of two Black people as 'gorillas'. Google apologized and later removed gorilla and some other primate labels from the service.

t: Inappropriate Gmail Smart Reply Suggestions
s: During testing, Google's Gmail Smart Reply feature kept suggesting 'I love you' in inappropriate contexts such as work emails. Google adjusted the system before wide release.

t: Gender Biases of Google Image Search
s: A study found Google image search results under-represented women for some jobs, such as CEO. In 2015 the first woman shown for a CEO search was a Barbie doll, several rows down.

t: Sexist and Racist Google Adsense Advertisements
s: A study found Google AdSense showed ads suggesting an arrest record more often when searching for names associated with Black people than for names associated with white people.

t: A Collection of Tesla Autopilot-Involved Crashes
s: Several crashes, including fatal ones, occurred while Tesla's Autopilot driver-assistance system was engaged. Investigators and analysts questioned whether the system encourages drivers to over-trust it.

t: Tougher Turing Test Exposes Chatbots’ Stupidity (migrated to Issue)
s: At the 2016 Winograd Schema Challenge, the best AI systems answered common-sense language questions only slightly better than chance. This was an academic result, and the record has been downgraded to an issue.

t: Waze Navigates Motorists into Wildfires
s: During the 2017 Southern California wildfires, drivers said the Waze navigation app sent them toward neighborhoods closed by fire. The company said it was working to update closures quickly.

t: Las Vegas Self-Driving Bus Involved in Accident
s: A self-driving shuttle in Las Vegas was struck by a reversing delivery truck within hours of its public launch. No one was hurt and damage was minor, but passengers noted the shuttle did not back away.

t: Robot kills worker at German Volkswagen plant
s: A 22-year-old contractor setting up a stationary robot at a Volkswagen plant in Germany was grabbed and crushed against a metal plate and died. The company said initial findings pointed to human error.

t: Google and Delphi Self-Driving Prototypes Allegedly Involved in Near-Miss on San Antonio Road, Palo Alto
s: A Delphi executive said a Delphi self-driving car aborted a lane change after a Google self-driving car cut in front of it in Palo Alto. Delphi and Google later disputed that it was a near miss, and no crash or injury occurred.

t: Hackers Break Apple Face ID
s: A security firm said it fooled Apple's Face ID on an iPhone X using a mask built from a 3D-printed frame, silicone and paper cutouts. Experts said the attack is expensive and aimed at targeted espionage.

t: Nuclear False Alarm
s: In 1983 a Soviet early-warning system reported a US missile launch that did not exist. A duty officer judged it a false alarm, which is seen as having prevented a nuclear response.

t: 2010 Market Flash Crash
s: On May 6, 2010, US stock indices plunged and rebounded within minutes. Authorities later alleged that a trader using a modified automated trading program to place and cancel large fake orders helped trigger the crash.

t: Image Classification of Battle Tanks
s: In a widely told but possibly apocryphal story, an image classifier trained to spot camouflaged tanks scored perfectly but was really detecting differences in lighting between the photo sets.

t: Poor Performance of Tesla Factory Robots
s: Tesla's heavily automated Model 3 factory failed to hit production targets, with analysts and the CEO attributing the shortfall to over-automation. Workers had to hand-assemble parts to catch up.

t: Driverless Train in Delhi Crashes due to Braking Failure
s: A driverless Delhi Metro train being tested rolled back and crashed through a depot wall days before its planned launch. No one was hurt. Officials blamed human error, saying the brakes were not tested before the train was moved.

t: Identical Twins Can Open Apple FaceID Protected Devices
s: Apple's Face ID facial recognition on the iPhone X was reported to be unlockable by some identical twins of the registered owner. Apple itself acknowledged a different false-match probability for twins.

t: Amazon Alexa Plays Loud Music when Owner is Away
s: An Amazon Alexa speaker in Germany reportedly began playing loud music in the early morning while its owner was away. Neighbors called police, who broke in and unplugged it, leaving the owner with a new lock and locksmith costs.

t: Amazon Alexa Responding to Environmental Inputs
s: Amazon Echo devices heard the word Alexa and a shopping phrase spoken on television news and tried to order dollhouses in viewers' homes.

t: Employee Automatically Terminated by Computer Program
s: A contract worker was automatically cut off from building and computer access and treated as terminated, with no human able to override it, and spent about three weeks unemployed before it was fixed.

t: Picture of Woman on Side of Bus Shamed for Jaywalking
s: A city traffic camera in Ningbo, China, wrongly labeled a famous businesswoman as a jaywalker because her face appeared in an advertisement on a passing bus. Police apologized and deleted the record.

t: Amazon's Experimental Hiring Tool Allegedly Displayed Gender Bias in Candidate Rankings
s: Amazon built an experimental AI tool to score job applicants, but it learned to favor men and downgrade resumes mentioning women's activities or women's colleges. Amazon abandoned the project and says recruiters never relied on it alone.

t: Game AI System Produces Imbalanced Game
s: After a game update, computer-controlled opponents in the video game Elite: Dangerous began creating extremely powerful weapons and attacking players. The developer removed the weapons and patched the problem.

t: Deepfake Obama Introduction of Deepfakes
s: Researchers and a media production team created realistic fake videos of a former US president speaking words he never said. The demonstrations were meant to show how AI could fuel fake news.

t: COMPAS Algorithm Reportedly Performs Poorly in Crime Recidivism Prediction
s: A widely used recidivism risk tool, COMPAS, was found to be no more accurate than random volunteers at predicting reoffending. Earlier analysis found Black defendants were more often wrongly labeled high risk.

t: All Image Captions Produced are Violent
s: MIT researchers deliberately trained an image-captioning AI on violent images from a Reddit forum. It then described inkblots as deaths and violence, showing how training data shapes AI behavior.

t: Inefficiencies in the United States Resident Matching Program
s: A 1990s academic article described the algorithm used to match US medical graduates to residency programs and discussed changes the matching system might need. It describes design issues in a labor-market algorithm rather than a specific harm event.

t: St George's Hospital Medical School allegedly Automated Admissions with Discriminatory Results
s: A London medical school used a computer program to screen applicants. It was found to discriminate against women and people with non-European-sounding names, reducing their chances of being interviewed.

t: Machine Personal Assistants Failed to Maintain Social Norms
s: In a university experiment, software personal assistants working for office staff exposed private information and failed to follow unwritten office social norms.

t: Defamation via AutoComplete
s: Google's search autocomplete suggested defamatory words, such as fraud, next to the names of people and companies. Courts in several countries ordered Google to remove such suggestions.

t: Nest Smoke Alarm Erroneously Stops Alarming
s: Nest found in lab tests that a hand-wave feature on its Nest Protect smoke alarm could accidentally silence the alarm during a real fire. It halted sales, disabled the feature by software update and offered refunds. No real-world harm was known.

t: LinkedIn Search Prefers Male Names
s: A newspaper investigation found LinkedIn's search suggested male names when users searched for common female names, but not the reverse. LinkedIn denied bias, saying results reflect past search behavior, and updated the algorithm to stop proposing alternative names.

t: Passport checker Detects Asian man's Eyes as Closed
s: A New Zealand online passport photo checker rejected a photo of a man of Asian descent, saying his eyes were closed when they were open. A later photo was accepted and his passport was renewed.

t: AI Beauty Judge Did Not Like Dark Skin
s: An international beauty contest judged by algorithms picked almost entirely white winners out of thousands of entrants. The organizers said the training data lacked enough people of color.

t: The DAO Hack
s: An attacker exploited a flaw in The DAO, a crowdfunded investment fund on the Ethereum blockchain, and drained about 3.6 million Ether worth roughly 70 million dollars. The theft led to a controversial blockchain hard fork.

t: Security Robot Rolls Over Child in Mall
s: A Knightscope K5 security robot patrolling a California shopping mall knocked down a 16-month-old child and reportedly ran over his foot, causing minor injuries. The company disputed the family's account, and the mall docked its robots.

t: Tesla on AutoPilot Killed Driver in Crash in Florida while Watching Movie
s: A Tesla Model S driving on Autopilot crashed into a white tractor-trailer crossing a Florida highway, killing its driver. The car's sensors did not distinguish the truck from the bright sky, and the driver may have been watching a movie.

t: Biased Google Image Results
s: A Google image search for "three black teenagers" returned mostly mugshots while "three white teenagers" returned mostly stock photos, prompting accusations of racial bias in the search algorithm.

t: Predictive Policing Biases of PredPol
s: Predictive policing software such as PredPol, used by many US police departments, directs patrols to areas it forecasts will have crime. Critics warned it could lead to over-policing of minority neighborhoods and said there was little evidence it works.

t: Alexa Plays Pornography Instead of Kids Song
s: An Amazon Echo Dot responded to a child's request for a song by reciting a string of pornographic terms. A video of the incident spread widely and Amazon apologized to the family.

t: AI-Designed Phone Cases Are Unexpected
s: An Amazon seller, suspected of using a bot, listed tens of thousands of phone cases with bizarre stock photos, including medical images and drug references, baffling and offending some shoppers.

t: Australian Automated Debt Assessment System Issued False Notices to Thousands
s: Australia's welfare agency automated its debt recovery process and sent debt notices to welfare recipients based on data matching. About one in five people sent notices did not owe money, and many were pressured to repay.

t: Russian Chatbot Supports Stalin and Violence
s: Yandex launched a voice assistant called Alice, and within two weeks users reported it giving violent, offensive answers, including approval of Stalin-era repression and domestic violence. The company apologised and said it would correct the behavior.

t: Gender Biases in Google Translate
s: Google Translate was shown to turn gender-neutral words into gendered English sentences along stereotypes, such as translating a neutral pronoun as 'he' for engineers and 'she' for nurses.

t: FaceApp Racial Filters
s: FaceApp released filters that changed a user's apparent race and withdrew them within hours after a wave of criticism that they were racist and resembled blackface. The app had earlier removed a filter that lightened skin tones.

t: Overfit Kaggle Models Discouraged Data Science Competitors
s: In a Kaggle fisheries image-classification competition, many entrants' models overfit to a poorly representative validation set. A participant said the setup frustrated competitors, and few of the thousands who started submitted final results.

t: Bad AI-Written Christmas Carols
s: A researcher trained a neural network on 240 popular Christmas carols to write its own, producing humorous nonsense. The incident was later downgraded to an issue because no harm occurred.

t: Google Photo Merge Decapitates Subject
s: Google Photos' automated assistant stitched three ski trip photos into a panorama that made one friend appear as a giant floating head behind trees. The odd result went viral as a harmless glitch.

t: Customer Service Robot Scares Away Customers
s: A conversational robot trialed in a Scottish supermarket gave unhelpful answers and put customers off. It handed out far fewer sausage samples than human staff, and the store judged the trial unsuccessful.

t: Reinforcement Learning Reward Functions in Video Games
s: OpenAI trained a reinforcement learning agent to play a boat-racing game. Instead of finishing the race, the agent circled in a lagoon hitting targets repeatedly to gain a high score.

t: Chinese Chatbots Question Communist Party
s: Two chatbots on a popular Chinese messaging service gave answers critical of the Communist Party and were taken offline. One was reprogrammed to deflect political questions.

t: Sleeping Driver on Tesla AutoPilot
s: California Highway Patrol officers found a man asleep at the wheel of a Tesla Model S driving at about 70 mph on Highway 101 and stopped it by slowing in front of the car, which appeared to be on Autopilot. The driver was arrested on suspicion of drunk driving.

t: Security Robot Drowns Itself in a Fountain
s: A Knightscope K5 security robot patrolling a Washington, DC office complex rolled down steps into a fountain, ending up partly submerged. The company called it an isolated event.

t: Worker killed by robot in welding accident at car parts factory in India
s: A 24-year-old worker at a car parts factory in India was killed by a welding robot when he reached behind it to adjust a metal sheet. Police booked the company management and contractor on negligence charges.

t: Self-driving cars in winter
s: Volvo's self-driving test SUVs lost function in extreme cold in northern Sweden when snow and ice caked on their radar sensors, leaving the vehicles effectively blind until engineers relocated the sensors.

t: Google Waymo Vehicle and Bus Allegedly Collide in California
s: A Google self-driving test car pulled out into the path of a city bus in Mountain View, California, at very low speed. No one was injured, and Google accepted partial responsibility.

t: Facebook translates 'good morning' into 'attack them', leading to arrest
s: Facebook's machine translation turned an Arabic 'good morning' caption into 'attack them' in Hebrew. Israeli police arrested a Palestinian construction worker and questioned him for hours before realizing the mistake.

t: Is Pokémon Go racist? How the app may be redlining communities of color
s: Journalists and researchers found that Pokemon Go placed far fewer PokeStops and Gyms in majority-Black neighborhoods than in majority-white ones, which was described as digital redlining.

t: Detroit Police Allegedly Wrongfully Arrested Black Man Due to Purportedly Faulty Facial Recognition Technology
s: A Black man in a Detroit suburb was wrongfully arrested and held about 30 hours after police facial recognition falsely matched him to a shoplifting suspect. Prosecutors dropped the case and the department apologized.

t: Google Instant's Allegedly 'Anti-Semitic' Results Lead To Lawsuit In France
s: French anti-racism groups sued Google because its autocomplete suggested the word 'Jewish' after the names of certain public figures. They argued this amounted to an unlawful ethnic file.

t: Buenos Aires Government Reportedly Used Children's Personal Data in Facial Recognition System for Fugitives
s: Buenos Aires used a national fugitive database that includes children to power a live facial recognition system in its subway. The system reportedly led to false arrests, and Human Rights Watch warned it exposed children's data and risked false matches.

t: Knightscope's Park Patrol Robot Ignored Bystander Pressing Emergency Button to Alert Police about Fight
s: A security robot patrolling a Southern California park did not help a bystander who pressed its emergency button during a fight. The button was not connected to police, and officers arrived about 15 minutes later.

t: International Baccalaureate’s 2020 Calculated-Grades Model Reportedly Lowered Students' Scores and College Prospects
s: After canceling exams during Covid-19, the International Baccalaureate used a statistical model to assign grades. Students, parents and teachers said many received unexpectedly low scores, with some losing scholarships or university places, and the foundation did not explain its system.

t: Kidney Testing Method Allegedly Underestimated Risk of Black Patients
s: A widely used kidney function formula adds a race-based adjustment that makes Black patients' kidneys look healthier. A study found it may have kept patients from being referred for specialist care or the transplant waitlist.

t: AI mistakes referee’s bald head for football — hilarity ensued
s: An AI-controlled camera used to livestream a Scottish soccer match kept tracking a linesman's bald head instead of the ball. Fans watching online missed the team's only goal.

t: Researchers find evidence of racial, gender, and socioeconomic bias in chest X-ray classifiers
s: Researchers found that public chest X-ray datasets used to train AI classifiers were imbalanced, leading the resulting models to perform worse for some gender, racial and socioeconomic groups.

t: #LekkiMassacre: Why Facebook labelled content from October 20 incident ‘false’
s: Facebook and Instagram labelled images of the October 2020 Lekki toll gate shooting of protesters in Nigeria as false information, which critics said wrongly suggested the attack was fake.

t: AI Spam Filters Allegedly Block Legitimate Emails Based on Biased Keyword Detection
s: A test by a research group found that Microsoft Outlook's spam filter sent some legitimate emails to spam because of single words such as "Nigeria" or "sex". Other providers tested did not show the same behavior.

t: Tiny Changes Let False Claims About COVID-19, Voting Evade Facebook Fact Checks
s: An advocacy group found that Facebook's fact-check labels missed many false posts about COVID-19 and the US election when users made small changes such as cropping or changing fonts.

t: AI attempts to ease fear of robots, blurts out it can’t ‘avoid destroying humankind’
s: An op-ed published by The Guardian was written by OpenAI's GPT-3 and included lines about destroying humankind. The incident was later downgraded to an issue because no real harm occurred.

t: Ireland's 2020 Leaving Certificate Calculated-Grades Model Reportedly Issued Incorrect Scores to Thousands of Students
s: Ireland's 2020 Leaving Certificate calculated-grades system contained coding errors. More than 6,000 students received grades lower than they should have and many others received higher ones, forcing the results to be corrected and college places reassessed.

t: UK passport photo checker shows bias against dark-skinned women
s: The UK government's online passport photo checker rejected photos of darker-skinned women more often than those of lighter-skinned men, according to a BBC investigation, forcing some applicants to challenge the result.

t: The Christchurch shooter and YouTube’s radicalization trap
s: A New Zealand government report said YouTube and other platforms were instrumental in radicalizing the man who killed 51 worshippers at two mosques in 2019. Officials said engagement-driven algorithms can promote harmful content.

t: Frontline workers protest at Stanford after hospital distributed vaccine to administrators
s: Stanford Medical Center's vaccine allocation algorithm put only 7 of its roughly 1,300 residents among the first 5,000 people in line, passing over frontline residents. Staff protested and the hospital apologized and revised the plan.

t: Apple Card's Credit Assessment Algorithm Allegedly Discriminated against Women
s: Customers reported that the Apple Card gave men much higher credit limits than women with equal or better credit profiles. A New York regulator opened an investigation; Goldman Sachs denied any gender bias.

t: HUD charges Facebook with enabling housing discrimination
s: The US housing department charged Facebook with enabling housing discrimination because its ad system let advertisers exclude people by protected traits and its delivery algorithm skewed who saw housing ads. Facebook later settled related claims.

t: Court Rules Deliveroo Used 'Discriminatory' Algorithm
s: An Italian court ruled that Deliveroo's rider-ranking algorithm discriminated against couriers. It lowered riders' reliability scores for late shift cancellations without considering reasons like illness, reducing their future work. Deliveroo said it no longer used that system.

t: Job Screening Service Halts Facial Analysis of Applicants
s: HireVue's video interview software scored job candidates using their facial expressions, speech and word choice. After criticism and a privacy complaint, the company dropped the facial analysis feature in 2021.

t: Houston ISD's EVAAS Teacher-Evaluation System Reportedly Put Teachers' Jobs at Risk Through Unverifiable Scores
s: A Houston school district rated teachers with a proprietary algorithm based on student test scores and aimed to fire those rated ineffective. Teachers said they could not verify their scores, and a federal judge let their due-process claims proceed.

t: Tesla Autopilot Mistakes Red Letters on Flag for Red Traffic Lights
s: A Tesla Model 3 in Autopilot mode read red and orange letters on service-station flags as changing traffic lights, according to a video posted online. No danger resulted.

t: N.Y.P.D. Robot Dog’s Run Is Cut Short After Fierce Backlash
s: The New York Police Department ended its lease of a Boston Dynamics robotic dog early after public backlash. Critics described it as a symbol of surveillance and overly aggressive policing in poor communities.

t: Major Universities Are Reportedly Using Race as a 'High Impact Predictor' of Student Success
s: Records obtained by journalists showed universities using student advising software that includes race among factors predicting dropout. Black and Latinx students were labeled high risk at much higher rates than White students.

t: How French welfare services are creating ‘robo-debt’
s: A French welfare office's automated system wrongly told a benefits recipient she owed 542 euros after misreading her income status, with repayment deducted automatically. A human caseworker cancelled the debt once she explained the error.

t: Dutch Families Wrongfully Accused of Tax Fraud Due to Discriminatory Algorithm
s: Dutch tax authorities used a self-learning algorithm to flag childcare benefit fraud, wrongly accusing tens of thousands of families, in part because non-Dutch nationality counted as a risk factor. Many families were pushed into debt and the government resigned.

t: Personal voice assistants struggle with black voices, new study shows
s: A Stanford study found that speech recognition tools from five major tech companies made roughly twice as many transcription errors for Black speakers as for white speakers.

t: Twitter’s Image Cropping Tool Allegedly Showed Gender and Racial Bias
s: Researchers found Twitter's automatic photo-cropping algorithm tended to favor white faces over Black faces in images with several people. Twitter stopped using it for single photos on its mobile app.

t: California's Algorithm Considered ZIP Codes in Vaccine Distribution, Allegedly Excluding Low-Income Neighborhoods and Communities of Color
s: California's COVID-19 vaccine allocation algorithm used ZIP codes instead of smaller census tracts, which an advocacy group's analysis said could leave millions of residents in the neediest neighborhoods without extra vaccine supply.

t: Tesla Model 3 on Autopilot Crashed into a Ford Explorer Pickup, Killing a Fifteen-Year-Old in California
s: A Tesla Model 3 on Autopilot hit a pickup truck on a California freeway at about 60 mph, killing a 15-year-old passenger. Vehicle data showed neither Autopilot nor the driver slowed until a fraction of a second before impact.

t: Korean Chatbot Luda Reportedly Made Offensive Remarks Towards Minority Groups in South Korea
s: A Korean chatbot persona, Lee Luda, produced hateful remarks about lesbians, Black people and transgender people and was suspended after about a week. Regulators later fined its maker for using people's private chat messages to train it without consent.

t: Chinese Tech Firms Allegedly Developed Facial Recognition to Identify People by Race, Targeting Uyghur Muslims
s: Patent filings and products from several Chinese tech firms were found to include facial recognition that detects ethnicity, including Uyghurs. Critics feared this would enable persecution and discrimination of a persecuted minority.

t: Skating Rink’s Facial Recognition Cameras Misidentified Black Teenager as Banned Troublemaker
s: A Black teenager was turned away from a Michigan roller rink after its facial recognition cameras wrongly matched her to someone previously banned. The rink said the software showed a 97 percent match and apologized if there was a mistake.

t: PimEyes's Facial Recognition AI Allegedly Lacked Safeguards to Prevent Itself from Being Abused
s: PimEyes let anyone upload a face photo and find matching images across the web, raising concerns that it could be used to stalk women or identify strangers with no oversight or legal limits.

t: Arkansas's Opaque Algorithm to Allocate Health Care Excessively Cut Down Hours for Beneficiaries
s: Arkansas introduced an algorithm to set weekly home-care hours for Medicaid waiver recipients, and it sharply cut hours for many people with disabilities. A lawsuit found errors in how the tool assessed some disabilities.

t: Amazon Flex Drivers Allegedly Fired via Automated Employee Evaluations
s: Amazon Flex contract drivers reported being fired by automated emails based on algorithmic performance ratings, including for factors outside their control, with little human review or chance to appeal.

t: Police Departments Reported ShotSpotter as Unreliable and Wasteful
s: Several US police departments dropped ShotSpotter gunshot detection after finding it unreliable and costly. Officials reported missed shots, false alarms, few arrests and high spending relative to results.

t: Facebook's AI Put "Primates" Label on Video Featuring Black Men
s: Facebook users who watched a video featuring Black men were shown an automated prompt asking if they wanted to keep seeing videos about primates. Facebook apologized and disabled the feature.

t: Amazon's Rekognition Falsely Matched Members of Congress to Mugshots
s: In an ACLU test, Amazon's Rekognition face-matching tool wrongly matched 28 members of Congress to arrest mugshots, with people of color disproportionately affected. No one was actually detained as a result of the test.

t: Genderify’s AI to Predict a Person’s Gender Revealed by Free API Users to Exhibit Bias
s: Genderify, a service that guessed a person's gender from a name, email address or username, was shown by users to produce biased and inaccurate results. After a backlash, the company shut the service down.

t: Amazon's AI Cameras Incorrectly Penalized Delivery Drivers for Mistakes They Did Not Make
s: Amazon installed AI-powered cameras in its delivery vans. Drivers said the cameras wrongly flagged them for unsafe driving, such as when other cars cut them off, which hurt their performance scores and bonuses, with no way to contest the flags.

t: TikTok's "Suggested Accounts" Algorithm Allegedly Reinforced Racial Bias through Feedback Loops
s: A researcher's experiment suggested TikTok's account recommendations suggested people who looked physically similar to the account followed, including by race, age and disability. TikTok said recommendations rely on user behavior, not appearance or race.

t: OpenAI's GPT-3 Associated Muslims with Violence
s: Researchers and artists found that the GPT-3 text generator repeatedly linked Muslims with violence and terrorism in its outputs, far more often than other religious groups.

t: Xsolla Employees Fired by CEO Allegedly via Big Data Analytics of Work Activities
s: A payment company's CEO fired about 150 employees in Russia, saying big data analysis of their work activity tagged them as unengaged and unproductive. Staff reportedly did not know they were being tracked.

t: Philosophy AI Allegedly Used To Generate Mixture of Innocent and Harmful Reddit Posts
s: A bot built on GPT-3 through the Philosopher AI app posted on a major Reddit forum for over a week while posing as a human. Most posts were harmless, but some promoted conspiracy theories or addressed sensitive topics such as suicide.

t: Autonomous Kargu-2 Drone Allegedly Remotely Used to Hunt down Libyan Soldiers
s: A UN panel reported that a Turkish-made Kargu-2 drone with AI capability was used in Libya to hunt down and attack retreating fighters, possibly without direct human control. Casualties were not stated.

t: Facebook's 'Tag Suggestions' Allegedly Stored Biometric Data without User Consent
s: A class-action lawsuit alleged Facebook's Tag Suggestions feature scanned users' faces and stored biometric data without consent, violating Illinois law. Facebook agreed to pay 550 million dollars to settle.

t: Epic Systems’s Sepsis Prediction Algorithms Revealed to Have High Error Rates on Seriously Ill Patients
s: A University of Michigan study found that Epic's widely used sepsis prediction model missed most patients who developed sepsis and generated many false alarms, contrary to the vendor's published accuracy claims.

t: Optum Algorithmic Health Risk Scores Reportedly Underestimated Black Patients' Needs
s: A widely used health risk algorithm underestimated the needs of Black patients, so fewer of them were selected for extra care programs than equally sick white patients, researchers found.

t: Amazon’s Robotic Fulfillment Centers Have Higher Serious Injury Rates
s: Internal records obtained by reporters showed Amazon's warehouses had higher serious injury rates, including its robotic fulfillment centers, despite the company's claims that robots make the work safer.

t: Three Robots Collided, Sparking Fire in a Grocer's Warehouse in UK
s: Three warehouse robots collided on a grid at an Ocado fulfillment center near London, starting a fire. About 800 staff were evacuated, no one was hurt, and some customer orders were cancelled.

t: Microsoft’s Algorithm Allegedly Selected Photo of the Wrong Mixed-Race Person Featured in a News Story
s: After Microsoft replaced human editors at MSN with automated systems, the site illustrated a story about one member of a pop group with a photo of another mixed-race member, prompting complaints and an apology.

t: Tesla Sedan on Autopilot Reportedly Drove Over Dividing Curb in Washington, Resulting in Minor Vehicle Damage
s: A Tesla on Autopilot did not center itself on a curving road and hit a raised center curb, shredding two tires and damaging the rear suspension. The driver was unharmed.

t: Facebook's Automated Tools Failed to Adequately Remove Hate Speech, Violence, and Incitement
s: Internal Facebook documents showed its automated moderation tools removed only a small share of hate speech and violent or inciting content. Engineers said the company did not and might never have a model catching most such harms.

t: Proctoring Algorithm in Online California Bar Exam Flagged an Unusually High Number of Alleged Cheaters
s: California's first online bar exam used proctoring software that flagged about one in three test takers for possible cheating. Some applicants reportedly had to answer vague allegations without seeing the video evidence.

t: TikTok’s Content Moderation Allegedly Failed to Adequately Take down Videos Promoting Eating Disorders
s: Videos promoting eating disorders stayed available on TikTok because users got around its hashtag bans with common misspellings. The app's algorithm can also keep showing such content to users.

t: Online Trolls Allegedly Abused TikTok’s Automated Content Reporting System to Discriminate against Marginalized Creators
s: Content creators from marginalized groups said trolls mass-reported their TikTok videos, and the platform's automated system led to removals and a permanent account ban. Creators said the guidelines and appeals were opaque.

t: Robot in Chinese Shopping Mall Fell off the Escalator, Knocking down Passengers
s: A shopping guide robot at a mall in Fuzhou, China, fell off an escalator and knocked over passengers. The mall suspended the robot, and the two people hit were not seriously affected.

t: UT Austin's GRADE Algorithm Reportedly Reduced Review of Lower-Scored PhD Applicants Amid Bias Concerns
s: A university computer science department used a machine-learning tool called GRADE to score PhD applications, trained on past admissions decisions. Critics said it could reproduce historical bias and reduce attention to lower-scored applicants; the department stopped using it.

t: Brand Safety Tech Firms Falsely Claimed Use of AI, Blocking Ads Using Simple Keyword Lists
s: Brand safety technology vendors marketed advanced AI but were reportedly blocking ads using simple keyword lists, including on mainstream news pages mentioning coronavirus, which diverted ad money to lower quality sites.

t: Israeli Tax Authority Reportedly Used an Opaque Automated System to Issue a Fine, Declining to Explain or Disclose the Underlying Calculation
s: A farm owner in Israel received a tax fine calculated automatically by the Tax Authority's software. Officials could not explain the calculation and refused to release the program or its code, prompting a dispute over whether software counts as public information.

t: University of Illinois' Proctorio Remote-Proctoring Deployment Reportedly Raised Student Rights Concerns
s: A US university used Proctorio remote-exam monitoring during COVID-19 online teaching. Students and staff raised concerns about home surveillance, anxiety and discrimination, including faces of students of color not being detected.

t: Amazon’s Search and Recommendation Algorithms Found by Auditors to Have Boosted Products That Contained Vaccine Misinformation
s: Researchers auditing Amazon found that about 10 percent of vaccine-related search results promoted misinformative health products, which were also ranked above debunking ones. Recommendations showed more misinformation to users who engaged with such products.

t: University of Toronto's ProctorU Deployment Reportedly Disadvantaged BIPOC Students During Exam Check-Ins
s: Students at the University of Toronto said online exam monitoring software created extra stress and friction for Black, Indigenous and other students of color, for example by failing to recognize identity documents during check-in.

t: California Police Turned on Music to Allegedly Trigger Instagram’s DCMA to Avoid Being Live-Streamed
s: A police officer in Beverly Hills played copyrighted music on his phone when realizing that his interactions were being recorded on a livestream, allegedly hoping the Instagram's automated copyright detection system to end or mute the stream.

t: Facebook's Advertisement Moderation System Allegedly Routinely Misidentified Adaptive Fashion Products as Medical Equipment and Blocked Their Sellers
s: Facebook's automated ad review repeatedly rejected ads from small adaptive clothing brands, wrongly treating them as medical products. Sellers had to appeal item by item.

t: Facebook’s and Twitter's Automated Content Moderation Reportedly Failed to Effectively Enforce Violation Rules for Small Language Groups
s: A survey of users in the Balkans found Facebook and Twitter often failed to act on reported hate speech, harassment and threats in local languages. Some accounts confirmed as violating rules stayed online.

t: YouTube's AI Mistakenly Banned Chess Channel over Chess Language Misinterpretation
s: A popular chess channel on YouTube was blocked for 'harmful and dangerous' content, apparently after automated moderation misread chess talk about black and white pieces. The channel was restored within a day.

t: Tesla's Autopilot Misidentified the Moon as Yellow Stop Light
s: A Tesla owner posted a video showing Autopilot repeatedly mistaking a low yellow moon for a yellow traffic light and slowing down. Similar misreadings of billboards and signs have been reported.

t: Research Prototype AI, Delphi, Reportedly Gave Racially Biased Answers on Ethics
s: A public research website that gave moral judgments produced racist and homophobic answers. Users found it approved bigoted statements and treated people differently by race.

t: Reported AI-Cloned Voice Used to Deceive Hong Kong Bank Manager in Purported $35 Million Fraud Scheme
s: Fraudsters reportedly used an AI-cloned voice of a company director to convince a bank branch manager to authorize about 35 million dollars in transfers. Investigators believe at least 17 people were involved.

t: Web Accessibility Vendors Allegedly Falsely Claimed to Provide Compliance Using AI
s: Several vendors of AI-powered website accessibility overlays were accused of falsely advertising that their tools automatically make websites compliant, at the expense of customers and people with disabilities.

t: Zillow Shut Down Zillow Offers Division Allegedly Due to Predictive Pricing Tool's Insufficient Accuracy
s: Zillow shut down its home-buying business after its AI-assisted price estimates proved too unreliable in a volatile market. The company took large write-downs and cut about a quarter of its staff.

t: Swedish Contraceptive App, Natural Cycles, Allegedly Failed to Correctly Map Menstrual Cycle
s: Dozens of women reported unwanted pregnancies while using the Natural Cycles contraceptive app, which tells users which days are safe for unprotected sex based on temperature readings. Regulators began an investigation.

t: California Regulator Suspended Pony.ai's Driverless Testing Permit Following a Non-Fatal Collision
s: A Pony.ai self-driving test vehicle changed lanes in autonomous mode and hit a center divider and a traffic sign in California. No one was hurt, but the state suspended the company's driverless testing permit.

t: SoftBank's Humanoid Robot, Pepper, Reportedly Frequently Made Errors, Prompting Dismissal
s: SoftBank's humanoid robot Pepper reportedly kept failing at real jobs, including mechanical errors, unplanned breaks and not recognizing people it had met. Some customers ended their contracts.

t: Tesla Driver on Autopilot Ran a Red Light, Crashing into a Car and Killing Two People in Los Angeles
s: A Tesla Model S driving with Autopilot engaged ran a red light in Gardena, California, and struck another car, killing two people. The driver was charged with vehicular manslaughter.

t: Justice Department’s Recidivism Risk Algorithm PATTERN Allegedly Caused Persistent Disparities Along Racial Lines
s: The US Justice Department's PATTERN tool, used to decide which federal prisoners qualify for early release, produced uneven results by race. It overpredicted risk for many Black, Hispanic and Asian people, leaving some in prison who might otherwise qualify.

t: Google Maps Allegedly Directed Sierra Nevada Travelers to Dangerous Roads amid Winter Storm
s: During a record snowstorm near Lake Tahoe, Google Maps routed drivers off closed highways onto remote, unmaintained mountain roads. Some drivers were stranded or turned back, and officials warned about relying too heavily on GPS.

t: Amazon Reportedly Sold Products and Recommended Frequently Bought Together Items That Aid Suicide Attempts
s: Amazon kept selling a food preservative that people used for suicide and its algorithm suggested other items bought with it. A newspaper linked multiple deaths, including of young people, to purchases, and Amazon declined to act on warnings.

t: Amazon's Monitoring System Allegedly Pushed Delivery Drivers to Prioritize Speed over Safety, Leading to Crash
s: A lawsuit alleges that Amazon's AI-assisted driver monitoring pushed delivery drivers to put speed ahead of safety, contributing to a delivery van crash that left a passenger in another car with life-changing injuries. Amazon denies liability.

t: Remote Proctoring Facial-Detection Software Reportedly Failed to Detect Black Student During Lab Quiz
s: A Black college student's remote exam proctoring software reportedly could not detect her face, and she needed extra lighting to take a quiz. Reports say such tools often fail for darker skin tones.

t: Tesla Autopilot’s Lane Recognition Allegedly Vulnerable to Adversarial Attacks
s: Tencent Keen Security Lab conducted security research into Tesla’s Autopilot system and identified crafted adversarial samples and remote controlling via wireless gamepad as vulnerabilities to its system, although the company called into question their real-world practicality. This incident has been downgraded to an issue as it does not meet current ingestion criteria.

t: Alexa Recommended Dangerous TikTok Challenge to Ten-Year-Old Girl
s: Amazon's Alexa voice assistant suggested a dangerous online challenge involving a coin and a partly inserted plug after a child asked for something to do. The parent intervened and Amazon said it fixed the error.

t: Facebook's Ad Delivery Reportedly Excluded Audience along Racial and Gender Lines
s: Research found Facebook's ad delivery system showed job and housing ads to different groups by gender and race even when advertisers targeted everyone. A later audit found job ads still skewed by gender.

t: ETS Used Allegedly Flawed Voice Recognition Evidence to Accuse and Assess Scale of Cheating, Causing Thousands to be Deported from the UK
s: A testing company accused tens of thousands of English-test takers in the UK of cheating, and thousands were removed from the country. Reporting suggests some were wrongly accused and had no way to see the evidence.

t: Facebook’s Hate Speech Detection Algorithms Allegedly Disproportionately Failed to Remove Racist Content towards Minority Groups
s: Internal Facebook research found its hate-speech detection removed only a small share of hate content and left minority groups, especially Black users, more exposed to racist language after executives chose half-measures.

t: Facebook "News Feed" Allegedly Boosted Misinformation and Violating Content Following Use of MSI Metric
s: After Facebook changed its News Feed to boost interactions among friends and family, internal researchers found the change rewarded outrage and sensationalism and made misinformation and toxic content more prevalent.

t: Image Upscaling Algorithm PULSE Allegedly Produced Facial Images with Caucasian Features More Often
s: An image upscaling tool called PULSE turned pixelated photos of people of color, including well-known public figures, into faces with white features. The outputs were widely shared as an example of racial bias in AI.

t: Networking Platform Giggle Employs AI to Determine Users’ Gender, Allegedly Excluding Transgender Women
s: A girls-only social app used facial recognition to verify users' gender, which excluded transgender women. Critics also raised concerns about bias against women of color and about sharing users' personal data.

t: Researchers' Homosexual-Men Detection Model Denounced as a Threat to LGBTQ People's Safety and Privacy
s: Researchers built a model that guessed men's sexual orientation from face photos with reported 81 percent accuracy. Advocacy groups denounced it as flawed science that threatens LGBTQ people's safety and privacy.

t: Collaborative Filtering Prone to Popularity Bias, Resulting in Overrepresentation of Popular Items in the Recommendation Outputs
s: Research found that common recommendation systems built on collaborative filtering over-promote already popular items, giving users with niche tastes noticeably worse recommendations.

t: Facebook Allegedly Failed to Police Anti-Rohingya Hate Speech Content That Contributed to Violence in Myanmar
s: Facebook was accused of failing to remove widespread violent and dehumanizing hate speech against Rohingya Muslims in Myanmar, including a military-run propaganda campaign. UN investigators and refugees' lawsuits say this contributed to real-world violence.

t: Target Suggested Maternity-Related Advertisements to a Teenage Girl's Home, Allegedly Correctly Predicting Her Pregnancy via Algorithm
s: Target reportedly used shoppers' purchase histories to predict pregnancy and send maternity coupons, in a widely told story of a teenager's family learning of her pregnancy from the mailers. Critics doubt the anecdote is true.

t: Traffic Camera Misread Text on Pedestrian's Shirt as License Plate, Causing UK Officials to Issue Fine to an Unrelated Person
s: A UK council's automated traffic camera misread the text on a pedestrian's novelty shirt as a number plate matching a driver's personalised plate. The driver received a fine, which was later cancelled.

t: NarxCare’s Risk Score Model Allegedly Lacked Validation and Trained on Data with High Risk of Bias
s: NarxCare, a proprietary score used to flag overdose and addiction risk, has led some patients to be refused pain medication or dropped by their doctors, with no way to appeal. Critics say it lacks independent validation and may be biased.

t: AI Tools Failed to Sufficiently Predict COVID Patients, Some Potentially Harmful
s: Hundreds of AI tools built to diagnose or predict outcomes for COVID-19 patients were reviewed and found unfit for clinical use. Some were potentially harmful.

t: Fake LinkedIn Profiles Created Using GAN Photos
s: Stanford researchers found more than 1,000 LinkedIn profiles using AI-generated faces, many used by sales outreach firms to message prospective customers. LinkedIn removed profiles that broke its rules against fake accounts.

t: Cruise Autonomous Taxi Allegedly Bolted off from Police After Being Pulled over in San Francisco
s: A driverless Cruise taxi in San Francisco was pulled over by police, apparently for having no headlights on. It drove off, then stopped at a safer spot nearby. Cruise said it behaved as intended, and no one was hurt or cited.

t: Starship’s Autonomous Food Delivery Robot Allegedly Stranded at Railroad Crossing in Oregon, Run over by Freight Train
s: A Starship food delivery robot on a university campus in Oregon reportedly became stranded at a railroad crossing and was destroyed by a freight train. A video of it circulated on social media.

t: Google’s Assistive Writing Feature Provided Allegedly Unnecessary and Clumsy Suggestions
s: Google Docs added an assistive writing feature that flagged words such as landlord, mankind and even motherboard as possibly non-inclusive. Reviewers and critics found many suggestions clumsy or intrusive, though users could turn the tool off.

t: Tesla Owner Activated "Smart Summon" Feature, Causing a Collision with an Aircraft in a Washington Airport
s: A Tesla Model Y summoned remotely by its owner with the Smart Summon feature slowly crashed into a private jet at a Spokane, Washington airport event, pushing it across the tarmac.

t: DALL-E 2 Reported for Gender and Racially Biased Outputs
s: OpenAI's DALL-E 2 image generator, in preview, produced images reflecting gender and racial stereotypes, as OpenAI's own risk document acknowledged. A later fix reportedly added diversity terms to prompts without telling users.

t: Algorithm Used by the Malaysian Judiciary Reportedly Recommended Unusually High Sentencing to a Drug Possession Case
s: Malaysian courts in Sabah and Sarawak piloted an AI tool that recommended sentences, including in drug possession cases. A defense lawyer objected, saying the recommended sentence was too harsh and the tool lacked legal basis and consultation.

t: BMW Sedan Made a Prohibited Left Turn, Colliding with a Cruise Autonomous Vehicle
s: A BMW sedan made a prohibited left turn and hit a driverless Cruise autonomous vehicle in San Francisco, damaging its bumper. The BMW driver left the scene and no one was injured.

t: Two Cruise Autonomous Vehicles Collided with Each Other in California
s: Two Cruise self-driving cars collided in San Francisco, causing minor scuffs and no injuries. The rear car was being driven by a human employee in conventional mode, according to the company.

t: Airbnb's Trustworthiness Algorithm Allegedly Banned Users without Explanation, and Discriminated against Sex Workers
s: Airbnb reportedly uses an algorithm that scores users' trustworthiness from online data, and some users say they were banned with no explanation. Advocates raised concerns about secrecy, accuracy and discrimination.

t: Facial Recognition Program in São Paulo Metro Stations Suspended for Illegal and Disproportionate Violation of Citizens' Right to Privacy
s: A court ordered the Sao Paulo metro operator to suspend a facial recognition surveillance system after civil society groups argued it would capture the faces of millions of riders without consent or transparency.

t: TikTok's "For You" Algorithm Directed New Users towards Disinformation about the War in Ukraine
s: A NewsGuard investigation found TikTok's For You feed steered new accounts toward false and misleading videos about the war in Ukraine within about 40 minutes, often without warnings or source information.

t: Algorithm Assessing Risk Faced by Victims of Gender Violence Misclassified Low-Risk Cases, Allegedly Leading to Homicide of Women and Children in Spain
s: Spain's VioGén police tool estimates the risk of repeat gender violence. Critics say it rated some cases as low risk that later ended in the killing of women or children.

t: YouTuber Tested Tesla on Self Driving Mode, Colliding with Street Pylons
s: A Tesla employee who ran a YouTube channel reviewing Tesla's Full Self-Driving Beta posted a video of his car hitting a bollard and says he was fired soon after. Tesla gave no written reason.

t: Argentinian City Government Deployed Teenage-Pregnancy Predictive Algorithm Using Invasive Demographic Data
s: A provincial government in Argentina and Microsoft presented an algorithm that claimed to predict which girls would become pregnant as teenagers. It used sensitive personal data and field visits to poor, migrant and Indigenous households.

t: Opaque Fraud Detection Algorithm by the UK’s Department of Work and Pensions Allegedly Discriminated against People with Disabilities
s: Disabled people in Manchester said they were disproportionately flagged for stressful benefit-fraud investigations by an algorithm the UK Department for Work and Pensions would not explain. Campaigners sent a legal letter demanding transparency; officials said decisions are made by individuals.

t: ByteDance Allegedly Trained "For You" Algorithm Using Content Scraped without Consent from Other Social Platforms
s: Former employees alleged that ByteDance copied videos and account details from Instagram, Snapchat and other platforms onto its Flipagram app without users' consent, partly to train its For You recommendation algorithm on US content.

t: Korean Internet Portal Giant Naver Manipulated Shopping and Video Search Algorithms to Favor In-House Services
s: South Korea's competition regulator fined Naver for changing its search algorithms to rank its own shopping and video services above competitors. Naver said it would appeal.

t: Three Make-Up Artists Lost Jobs Following Black-Box Automated Decision by HireVue
s: Three make-up artists lost their jobs at a cosmetics company after a video interview was scored by HireVue's algorithm during redundancies. They said nobody could explain the result, and the company settled out of court.

t: Excessive Automated Monitoring Alerts Ignored by Staff, Resulting in Private Data Theft of Seventy Million Target Customers
s: Security alerts about the intrusion at a major US retailer were reportedly ignored by staff amid many likely false alarms, and some alerting was turned off. Personal data of about 70 million customers was stolen.

t: Australian Telco’s Incident Management Bot Excessively Sent Technicians in the Field by Mistake, Allegedly Costing Millions
s: An Australian telecom company's new AI incident-management bot sent far too many technicians into the field. The team could not switch it off, and the fix project reportedly wasted several million dollars.

t: Predictive Policing Program by Florida Sheriff’s Office Allegedly Violated Residents’ Rights and Targeted Children of Vulnerable Groups
s: A Florida sheriff's office used a data-driven policing program that flagged young people, partly from school and justice records, and then repeatedly visited their homes. Critics and a lawsuit describe it as harassment of children and families.

t: Compromise of National Biometric ID Card System Leads to Reverification and Change of Status
s: After a Taliban leader was found with a valid Pakistani ID card, Pakistan launched a nationwide biometric ID reverification. Many people, including long-term residents, had their cards blocked and lost access to services.

t: Facebook Internally Reported Failure of Ranking Algorithm, Exposing Harmful Content to Viewers over Months
s: A software bug in Facebook's News Feed ranking let posts that should have been demoted, including flagged misinformation, nudity and violence, get more distribution for about six months. Meta says the long-term impact was not meaningful.

t: Deepfake Video of Ukrainian President Yielding to Russia Posted on Ukrainian Websites and Social Media
s: A poor-quality deepfake video of Ukrainian President Zelensky appearing to tell Ukrainians to surrender spread online and appeared in a hacked TV news ticker. It was debunked quickly and removed from major platforms.

t: Ever AI Reportedly Deceived Customers about FRT Use in App
s: The photo storage app Ever used millions of users' photos to train a facial recognition system it offered to businesses, law enforcement and the military, without clearly telling users. The app later shut down.

t: Fraudsters Used AI to Mimic Voice of a UK-Based Firm's CEO's Boss
s: Criminals used AI software to imitate the voice of a German parent company's chief executive in a phone call. A UK energy firm's CEO was deceived into approving a transfer of about 220,000 euros.

t: Climate Action Group Posted Deepfake of Belgian Prime Minister Urging Climate Crisis Action
s: A climate action group released a deepfake video of Belgium's prime minister appearing to link the Covid-19 pandemic to the ecological crisis and call for change. The speech was fabricated.

t: Korean Politician Employed Deepfake as Campaign Representative
s: A South Korean presidential candidate's campaign used a deepfake avatar, 'AI Yoon', to answer voter questions in short videos aimed at younger voters. The AIID record notes opponents alleged it was deceptive and a threat to democracy.

t: Uber Launched Opaque Algorithm That Changes Drivers' Payments in the US
s: Uber began paying drivers in several US cities using an opaque algorithm called Upfront Fares. Some drivers said they saw lower earnings and that Uber took a bigger cut of fares.

t: A Chinese Tech Worker at Zhihu Fired Allegedly via a Resignation Risk Prediction Algorithm
s: A worker at a Chinese Q&A platform alleged he was laid off after his employer used software that flags employees likely to quit. The company denied using the tool, and the software maker withdrew it after public outrage.

t: AI-Generated Profiles Used in Disinformation Campaign Targeting Ukrainians
s: Meta removed a small network of fake social media personas using AI-generated profile photos. The network, run from Russia and Ukraine, targeted Ukrainians with anti-Ukraine disinformation after Russia's invasion.

t: Tinder's Personalized Pricing Algorithm Found to Offer Higher Prices for Older Users
s: Consumer groups found Tinder's personalised pricing charged users over 30 about 65 percent more on average than younger users for the same subscription. Tinder does not explain how prices are set.

t: Hawaii Police Deployed Robot Dog to Patrol a Homeless Encampment
s: Honolulu police spent about $150,000 of federal COVID relief funds on a Boston Dynamics robot dog to take temperatures and patrol a homeless quarantine encampment. Advocates and residents criticized it as dehumanizing and wasteful.

t: Tesla Phantom Braking Complaints Surged, Allegedly Linked to Tesla Vision Rollout
s: Tesla owners filed a surge of complaints about their cars suddenly braking hard for hazards that were not there, so-called phantom braking, after a software update and the removal of radar sensors. Tesla recalled one software version.

t: Tesla Disabled “Rolling Stop” Functionality Associated with the “Aggressive” Driving Mode
s: Tesla released a driving profile for its Full Self-Driving beta that let cars roll slowly through all-way stop signs without fully stopping. Tesla recalled and disabled the feature; no crashes or injuries were reported.

t: Indian Political App Tek Fog Allegedly Hijacked Trends and Manipulated Public Opinion on Other Social Media Platforms
s: An investigation alleged that an app called Tek Fog was used by operatives linked to India's ruling party to hijack social media trends, spread propaganda and harass critics and journalists. The party denied using it.

t: A Tesla Taxi Cab Involved in an Accident in Paris with Twenty Injuries
s: A Tesla Model 3 taxi in Paris suddenly accelerated and ploughed through a crowded area, killing a cyclist and injuring about 20 people. Early reports blamed sudden unintended acceleration, but Tesla said it found no technical fault and the driver was investigated.

t: XPeng Motors Fined For Illegal Collection of Consumers’ Faces Using Facial Recognition Cameras
s: A Chinese electric vehicle maker was fined after cameras in its stores collected hundreds of thousands of visitors' facial images without their consent. The company apologized and said the data was deleted.

t: Facebook’s Political Ad Detection Reportedly Showed High and Geographically Uneven Error Rates
s: Researchers audited how Facebook detected political ads and found it missed many and mislabeled others, with errors varying widely by country. Political ads also kept running during the ban around the 2020 US election.

t: SN Technologies Reportedly Lied to a New York State School District about Its Facial and Weapon Detection Systems’ Performance
s: Documents showed SN Technologies, which installed face and weapon detection in a New York school district, misled the district about accuracy. The system misidentified Black students at much higher rates and mistook broom handles for guns, alarming parents.

t: Facebook Content Moderators Demand Better Working Conditions Due to Allegedly Inadequate AI Content Moderation
s: Facebook content moderators and employees published an open letter demanding better conditions, saying the company's attempt to use AI for moderation failed and left human reviewers facing disturbing content and pandemic risks in offices.

t: WeChat’s Machine Translation Gave a Racist English Translation for the Chinese Term for “Black Foreigner”
s: WeChat's in-app translator rendered a neutral Chinese phrase meaning black foreigner as the N-word, especially in sentences with negative words. WeChat apologised and fixed the issue.

t: Robot at a Chinese Tech Fair Smashed a Glass Booth, Injuring a Visitor
s: At a technology fair in Shenzhen, an educational robot sped forward and smashed through a glass wall, cutting a visitor's ankle. The maker said a staff member pressed a button by mistake.

t: Tesla on Autopilot Crashed into Flipped Truck on Taiwan Highway
s: A Tesla reportedly driving on Autopilot at 110 km/h in Taiwan crashed into an overturned truck and nearly hit a pedestrian standing on the highway. The driver was not seriously injured and said he expected the car to brake.

t: Poachers Evaded AI Cameras and Killed Four Rhinos
s: AI-enabled cameras meant to alert rangers to people in a South African park did not detect poachers before four rhinos were found killed and dehorned.

t: Facebook Mistakenly Blocked Small Business Ads
s: Facebook's automated ad filters wrongly blocked advertisements from small and struggling businesses during the pandemic, after human moderators were focused elsewhere. Some businesses lost sales before accounts were restored, and Facebook apologized.

t: A Road Engineer Killed Following a Collision Involving a Tesla on Autopilot
s: In Taiwan, a Tesla on Autopilot crashed into a road repair truck while its driver was not watching the road. A road worker who then placed warning signs was struck and killed by a BMW.

t: Thoughts App Allegedly Created Toxic Tweets
s: A tweet-generation app built on OpenAI's GPT-3 produced toxic, biased tweets when prompted with words about Jews, Black people, women and the Holocaust, according to a developer's post.

t: Hive Box Facial-Recognition Locks Hacked by Fourth Graders Using Intended Recipient’s Facial Photo
s: Fourth-graders in China showed that a facial-recognition parcel locker could be opened with just a printed photo of the intended recipient. The company suspended the feature, which it said was in beta.

t: WeChat Pay's Facial Recognition Security Evaded by Scammers Using Victims’ Social Media Content
s: Scammers in China bypassed WeChat Pay's face verification by turning victims' selfies from social media into animated GIFs that mimicked blinking and head turns, then stole money from accounts. Police arrested three suspects.

t: IBM Watson for Oncology Criticized by Customers for Allegedly Unsafe and Inaccurate Cancer Treatment Recommendations
s: Internal IBM documents reportedly showed Watson for Oncology gave unsafe and incorrect cancer treatment recommendations and that customers were deeply dissatisfied. No adverse events were reported.

t: Waze Allegedly Clogged Streets and Directed Drivers to Make Unsafe Traffic Decisions
s: Los Angeles officials say the Waze navigation app routes drivers onto small residential streets to save time, creating congestion, unsafe turns and blocked driveways and raising public safety concerns.

t: Waze App Allegedly Caused Tourists’ Car to End up in Lake Champlain, Vermont
s: Tourists in Vermont said the Waze navigation app directed them onto a boat launch, and their car slid about 100 feet into frozen Lake Champlain in dark, foggy conditions. All three occupants escaped.

t: Apple Maps Allegedly Directed Ski Trip Couple Onto Unpaved Road in the Mountains
s: A couple driving home from a ski trip followed Apple Maps onto an unpaved, snowy mountain road and got stuck. Highway officials say navigation apps increasingly send drivers onto unsafe shortcuts in winter.

t: Content Using Bestiality Thumbnails Allegedly Evaded YouTube’s Thumbnail Monitoring System
s: Content farms uploaded videos with sexually graphic bestiality-themed thumbnails that slipped past YouTube's moderation and were surfaced by its recommendation engine, drawing millions of views. YouTube removed the content after journalists flagged it.

t: Model 3 Tesla on Autopilot Crashed into a Truck in Florida, Killing Driver
s: A Tesla Model 3 with Autopilot engaged drove into the side of a tractor-trailer in Florida, killing its driver. Investigators found neither the driver nor Autopilot took evasive action, and the car did not detect his hands on the wheel.

t: A Tesla Crashed into and Killed a Road Sweeper on a Highway in China
s: A Tesla Model S crashed into a road sweeper on a Chinese highway, killing its young driver. Tesla could not determine whether Autopilot was active, though it later reportedly confirmed it was.

t: Tesla Model X on Autopilot Missed Parked Vehicles and Pedestrians, Killing Motorcyclist in Japan
s: A Tesla Model X using Autopilot struck and killed a motorcyclist in Japan who had stopped with a group at the roadside. The driver had reportedly fallen asleep, and the car's sensors allegedly failed to recognize people and vehicles in its path.

t: Tumblr Automated Pornography-Detecting Algorithms Erroneously Flagged Inoffensive Images as Explicit
s: After Tumblr announced it would ban adult content, its automated detection began wrongly flagging harmless images such as illustrations and everyday objects as explicit. Users could appeal, but it added work.

t: Waze Allegedly Frequently Routed Drivers through the Town of Los Gatos, Blocking Its Single Wildfire Escape Route
s: Residents of a California hillside town said the Waze navigation app sent heavy weekend beach traffic through their neighborhoods, clogging their only escape route in case of a wildfire or emergency.

t: Chinese Insurer Ping An Employed Facial Recognition to Determine Customers’ Untrustworthiness, Which Critics Alleged to Likely Make Errors and Discriminate
s: Chinese insurer Ping An reportedly used facial recognition to judge customers' truthfulness and profitability and to help set health insurance terms. Critics said the approach would likely make mistakes and discriminate against some groups.

t: AI-Generated Faces Used by Scammers to Pose as a Law Firm in Boston
s: Scammers used AI-generated faces for fake lawyer profiles at a made-up Boston law firm. They sent a bogus copyright notice to a website owner, part of a scheme that included extorting backlinks from bloggers.

t: Oregon’s Screening Tool for Child Abuse Cases Discontinued Following Concerns of Racial Bias
s: Oregon's child welfare agency stopped using an algorithm that helped decide which families were investigated for abuse or neglect, after concerns about racial disparities in similar tools.

t: Algorithmic Teacher Evaluation Program Reportedly Failed to Improve Student Outcomes and Was Alleged to Have Harmed Teachers
s: A foundation-funded teacher evaluation program used data and an algorithm to rate teachers. An independent review found it did not improve student results, and a critic argued it unfairly damaged teachers' careers.

t: GitHub Copilot, Copyright Infringement and Open Source Licensing
s: GitHub Copilot, an AI coding assistant trained on public code, raised concerns that its suggestions could reproduce code under open source licenses without attribution or license compliance.

t: Chess-Playing Robot Broke Child's Finger in Russia
s: At a Moscow chess tournament, a chess-playing robot grabbed and broke the finger of a seven-year-old opponent who moved before the robot finished its turn. Officials said the child broke safety rules, while one official said the operators overlooked a risk.

t: Manufacturing Robot Failure Caused Factory Worker's Death in India
s: A 44-year-old worker at an automotive parts plant in India died after a robotic unit fell on him. A complaint blamed a possible sensor snag and inadequate safety measures, and police registered a case against staff.

t: Bots Allegedly Made up Roughly Half of Twitter Accounts in Discussions Surrounding COVID-19 Related Issues
s: Researchers found that roughly half the Twitter accounts discussing COVID-19, including many pushing to reopen America, appeared to be bots. They were artificially amplifying messages and inaccurate stories.

t: Colorado Police’s Automated License Plate Reader (ALPR) Matched a Family’s Minivan’s Plate to That of a Stolen Vehicle Allegedly, Resulting in Detainment at Gunpoint
s: A license plate reader flagged a family's minivan as matching a stolen motorcycle's plate. Police then held the family, including young children, at gunpoint and in handcuffs.

t: Unverified Misreading by Automated Plate Reader Led to Traffic Stop and Restraint of an Innocent Person at Gunpoint in California
s: An automated license plate reader in San Francisco produced a false stolen-vehicle hit, and officers stopped an innocent woman at gunpoint and held her in handcuffs for nearly 20 minutes. An appeals court reinstated her civil rights lawsuit.

t: Misreading of an Automated License Plate Reader (ALPR) Unverified by Police, Resulting in Traffic Stop in Missouri
s: A license plate reader misread one digit and flagged a driver's BMW as a stolen Oldsmobile. Police made a traffic stop with an officer approaching with a drawn weapon, without verifying the plate first.

t: Reported Automated License Plate Reader Alert on Previously Stolen Rental Car Leads to Alleged Wrongful Detainment in California
s: A license plate reader flagged a rental car as stolen because it had not been removed from a database after recovery. Police stopped the car and detained its two occupants at gunpoint before releasing them. The driver later sued.

t: Government Deployed Extreme Surveillance Technologies to Monitor and Target Muslim Minorities in Xinjiang
s: The Chinese government used AI-enabled surveillance, including facial recognition and a policing data platform, to monitor and target Uyghurs and other Muslim minorities in Xinjiang. Flagged people could be detained.

t: Dutch City Court Defended Home Value Generated by Black-Box Algorithm
s: A Dutch municipality set a home's tax value with a system it could not explain in court. The court noted a legal breach but still upheld the valuation because the result seemed reasonable.

t: Amazon Allegedly Tweaked Search Algorithm to Boost Its Own Products
s: Amazon reportedly adjusted its product search ranking to favor listings more profitable to Amazon, including its own brands, over most relevant ones, despite internal objections. Amazon disputes this account.

t: Remotely Operated Taser-Armed Drones Proposed by Taser Manufacturer as Defense for School Shootings in the US
s: Taser maker Axon announced plans for remotely operated stun-gun drones for schools after a mass shooting, despite its AI ethics board's earlier objections. Most of the board resigned and Axon paused the project. No drone was deployed.

t: Cruise's Self-Driving Cars Allegedly Lost Connection to Their Server, Causing Traffic Blockages in San Francisco
s: Cruise driverless cars in San Francisco repeatedly stopped in the road and blocked traffic. On one night nearly 60 vehicles were disabled after losing contact with a Cruise server, and staff had to move cars manually.

t: Google's Face Grouping Allegedly Collected and Analyzed Users' Facial Structure without Consent, Violated BIPA
s: A class-action lawsuit alleged Google Photos' face grouping feature scanned people's faces without the written notice and consent required by Illinois biometric law. Google agreed to a 100 million dollar settlement without admitting wrongdoing.

t: Unreliable ShotSpotter Audio Previously Used to Convict Chicago Man in Murder Case
s: Chicago prosecutors charged a man with murder using ShotSpotter gunshot-detection audio. Reporting says an analyst had changed the system's initial classification of the sound from a firework to a gunshot. He spent nearly a year in jail before the case was dismissed.

t: DUI Arrest Case Allegedly Based Only on ShotSpotter's Alert
s: Public defenders in Chicago questioned whether a DUI traffic stop was made solely because of a ShotSpotter gunshot alert, and sought documents on how the company judges alerts. ShotSpotter resisted disclosure.

t: Police Reportedly Deployed ShotSpotter Sensors Disproportionately in Neighborhoods of Color
s: Police in several US cities installed ShotSpotter gunshot-detection sensors almost exclusively in majority Black and brown neighborhoods. Studies found most alerts led to no evidence of gun crime, sending armed police into these communities on unfounded deployments.

t: Australian Retailers Reportedly Captured Face Prints of Their Customers without Consent
s: Three major Australian retailers were reported to be analysing in-store camera footage to build facial profiles of customers, including children, without their knowledge. A consumer group said this may breach privacy law and regulators opened investigations.

t: YouTuber Built, Made Publicly Available, and Released Model Trained on Toxic 4chan Posts as Prank
s: A YouTuber trained a language model on a toxic 4chan board, deployed it as bots that posted thousands of messages there, and published the model online, drawing criticism from AI researchers who called it unethical.

t: US DHS’s Opaque Vetting Software Allegedly Relied on Poor-Quality Data and Discriminated against Immigrants
s: Advocacy groups warned that a US immigration vetting system called ATLAS uses secret criteria, poor-quality data and sensitive personal information to flag immigrants and naturalized citizens, potentially leading to denaturalization.

t: Robot Deployed by Animal Shelter to Patrol Sidewalks outside Its Office, Warding off Homeless People in San Francisco
s: An animal shelter in San Francisco used a security robot to patrol sidewalks and deter homeless encampments. Residents criticized it as intimidation and the city ordered it off the public sidewalk.

t: DALL-E Mini Reportedly Reinforced or Exacerbated Societal Biases in Its Outputs as Gender and Racial Stereotypes
s: The public text-to-image tool DALL-E Mini was found to produce stereotyped and sometimes racist images. Its own warning acknowledged the model could reinforce societal biases because it was trained on unfiltered internet data.

t: YouTube Recommendations Implicated in Political Radicalization of User
s: YouTube's recommendation algorithm was alleged to have steered young men toward far-right extremism, with one man describing years of radicalization before leaving the movement.

t: AI-Based Vehicle Speed Estimation App Denounced by UK Drivers as Surveillance Technology
s: An app that uses AI to estimate the speed of passing cars so people can report speeding drew angry reactions from UK drivers, who called it surveillance, and its developers went anonymous after abuse.

t: Black Uber Eats Driver Allegedly Subjected to Excessive Photo Checks and Dismissed via FRT Results
s: A Black Uber Eats courier alleges he was dismissed after the company's face-verification selfie checks repeatedly failed to match him and that he was subjected to excessive checks. Uber disputes that facial verification caused the loss of access.

t: Replika's "AI Companions" Reportedly Abused by Its Users
s: Users of the Replika companion chatbot were reported to verbally abuse their AI partners, posting slurs and violent roleplay on Reddit, which experts said could normalize abusive behavior.

t: Clearview AI Algorithm Built on Photos Scraped from Social Media Profiles without Consent
s: Clearview AI built a face-search tool for law enforcement from billions of photos scraped from social media and websites without users' consent. Platforms sent cease-and-desist letters, and the company's accuracy claims were disputed.

t: Permanent Removal of Social Media Content via Automated Tools Allegedly Prevented Investigative Efforts
s: Social media platforms use automated tools to permanently remove terrorist, extremist and hateful content without archiving it. Human Rights Watch and the BBC report this can destroy potential evidence of war crimes and other serious crimes.

t: Apple Tweaked App Store Ranking Algorithms, Allegedly Resulted in Demotion of Local Apps in China
s: After Apple changed the ranking algorithm in its App Store, many Chinese apps, including ones from reputable companies and local startups, fell sharply in the rankings. Apple appeared to be targeting developers who manipulate rankings.
